title: New Drug Shows Long-Term Promise for High Blood Pressure
subtitle: Recent findings suggest a daily pill could potentially cure a specific type of hypertension, offering a new alternative to surgery.

summary.en: A new medication called baxdrostat is showing surprising long-term results for patients with high blood pressure. While most treatments require daily use for life, this drug appears to provide benefits for years after patients stop taking it. The drug targets a specific hormone that causes blood pressure to rise. Researchers believe it may actually destroy the cells responsible for this hormone production. Larger studies are now underway to confirm if this treatment can serve as a permanent cure.
summary.zh: 一種名為 baxdrostat 的新藥在治療高血壓患者方面展現了令人驚訝的長期效果。雖然大多數治療需要終身每日服藥，但這種藥物似乎在患者停藥後仍能提供數年的療效。該藥物針對導致血壓升高的特定荷爾蒙。研究人員認為，它可能實際上摧毀了負責產生該荷爾蒙的細胞。目前更大規模的研究正在進行中，以確認這種療法是否能作為永久性的治癒手段。

paragraphs.en: Millions of people around the world live with high blood pressure, a condition that often requires lifelong daily medication to manage. However, a new drug called baxdrostat is offering fresh hope. Following recent reports on the drug’s potential, new findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine suggest that the treatment might do more than just manage symptoms—it could potentially cure a common cause of the condition.
paragraphs.zh: 全球有數百萬人患有高血壓，這種疾病通常需要終身每日服藥來控制。然而，一種名為 baxdrostat 的新藥帶來了新的希望。繼近期有關該藥物潛力的報導後，發表在《新英格蘭醫學期刊》（New England Journal of Medicine）上的最新研究結果顯示，這種療法可能不僅僅是控制症狀，還有潛力治癒導致該疾病的一種常見病因。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Health, the drug was originally designed to help patients whose blood pressure remained high despite using other existing medications. The condition, known as primary aldosteronism, affects roughly 5 to 10 percent of people with high blood pressure. It is caused by small, non-cancerous growths on the adrenal glands. These growths cause the body to produce too much of a hormone called aldosterone, which forces the kidneys to hold onto salt, leading to higher blood pressure.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）報導，該藥物最初是為了幫助那些即便使用現有藥物，血壓依然居高不下的患者所設計。這種被稱為原發性醛固酮增多症的病況，影響了約百分之五到十的高血壓患者。其成因是腎上腺上出現了小型非癌性增生。這些增生會導致身體產生過多的醛固酮荷爾蒙，迫使腎臟滯留鹽分，進而導致血壓升高。

paragraphs.en: Traditionally, the only way to treat this specific problem has been surgery to remove the affected gland. However, surgery is not always a perfect solution, as other factors often contribute to a patient's health issues. Baxdrostat works differently by acting as an aldosterone synthase inhibitor (ASI). This means it blocks the body from creating the hormone that raises blood pressure. While the drug was approved in the US earlier this year for difficult cases, its long-term effects were not fully understood until now.
paragraphs.zh: 傳統上，治療這種特定問題的唯一方法是進行手術切除受影響的腺體。然而，手術並不總是完美的解決方案，因為其他因素往往也會影響患者的健康狀況。Baxdrostat 的作用機制不同，它是一種醛固酮合成酶抑制劑。這意味著它能阻斷身體製造導致血壓升高的荷爾蒙。雖然該藥物今年稍早於美國獲准用於治療困難病例，但其長期影響直到現在才被充分理解。

paragraphs.en: In a small study, researchers followed 14 patients who took the daily pill for six to 12 months. After they stopped taking the medication, doctors were surprised to find that their blood pressure remained low for up to two years. Prof. Morris Brown, a hypertension specialist at Queen Mary University of London who led the study, described the results as very exciting. He noted that nearly one-quarter of the patients were able to stop all other treatments and maintain normal blood pressure levels.
paragraphs.zh: 在一項小型研究中，研究人員追蹤了十四名每日服用該藥物的患者，為期六到十二個月。在他們停止服藥後，醫生驚訝地發現，這些患者的血壓在長達兩年的時間內依然維持在低水平。領導這項研究的倫敦瑪麗皇后大學（Queen Mary University of London）高血壓專家莫里斯·布朗教授（Prof. Morris Brown）形容這些結果非常令人振奮。他指出，近四分之一的患者能夠停止所有其他治療，並維持正常的血壓水平。

paragraphs.en: Experts believe the drug may actually be killing the specific cells that cause the hormone imbalance. Prof. Brown explained that when the drug suppresses the hormone, it creates a reaction that may destroy the overactive cells. This theory is supported by older experiments in mice, which showed that removing the gene responsible for the hormone led to the loss of the cells that produced it. The team is currently conducting laboratory tests to confirm this mechanism.
paragraphs.zh: 專家認為，該藥物可能實際上殺死了導致荷爾蒙失調的特定細胞。布朗教授解釋說，當藥物抑制該荷爾蒙時，會產生一種反應，進而可能摧毀那些過度活躍的細胞。這項理論得到了早期小鼠實驗的支持，實驗顯示移除負責該荷爾蒙的基因，會導致產生該荷爾蒙的細胞消失。研究團隊目前正在進行實驗室測試，以確認此機制。

paragraphs.en: Despite these positive results, some medical experts are urging caution. Mason Freeman, a professor of medicine at Harvard University who participated in the research, noted that it is still too early to declare the patients fully cured. He emphasized that a larger trial is currently underway to see if these effects are common and if they last for a long time. If the results are confirmed, it could change how doctors diagnose and treat patients. Instead of invasive diagnostic procedures and surgery, doctors might simply use this drug to see if a patient responds well.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管有這些正面結果，一些醫學專家仍呼籲保持謹慎。參與該研究的哈佛大學（Harvard University）醫學教授梅森·弗里曼（Mason Freeman）指出，現在宣稱患者已完全治癒還為時過早。他強調，目前正在進行更大規模的試驗，以觀察這些效果是否普遍，以及是否能長期持續。如果結果獲得證實，這可能會改變醫生診斷和治療患者的方式。醫生或許不必再進行侵入性的診斷程序和手術，只需使用這種藥物來觀察患者的反應即可。

paragraphs.en: This development is particularly significant given the mixed results in the field of heart health recently. While other new drugs aimed at preventing heart disease have failed to show expected benefits, baxdrostat stands out for its potential to provide a lasting solution. The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) is currently assessing the drug, which could make it available through the NHS in the UK as early as next year.
paragraphs.zh: 這項進展在心臟健康領域近期結果好壞參半的情況下顯得尤為重要。雖然其他旨在預防心臟病的新藥未能展現預期的效益，但 baxdrostat 因其提供持久解決方案的潛力而脫穎而出。英國國家健康與照顧卓越研究院（National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, NICE）目前正在評估該藥物，這可能使其最快在明年透過英國國民保健署（NHS）提供給患者使用。

paragraphs.en: For now, the medical community remains cautiously optimistic. If the drug continues to perform as it has in early trials, it could represent a major shift in how we approach one of the world's most common health problems. By potentially removing the need for surgery and lifelong medication, baxdrostat could improve the quality of life for millions of people. For the moment, however, patients are advised to continue their current treatments until larger studies provide more definitive evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，醫學界仍保持審慎樂觀的態度。如果該藥物能持續展現早期試驗中的效果，它可能代表我們處理全球最常見健康問題的方式出現重大轉變。透過可能免除手術和終身服藥的需求，baxdrostat 有望改善數百萬人的生活品質。然而，現階段仍建議患者在更大規模的研究提供更確切的證據前，繼續目前的治療。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To keep or retain something rather than letting it go.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指腎臟將鹽分留在體內，而非排出。文中：which forces the kidneys to hold onto salt, leading to higher blood pressure.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be much better or more noticeable than other similar things.
keyTerms.noteZh: 指該藥物在眾多藥物中表現優異。文中：baxdrostat stands out for its potential to provide a lasting solution.

previousArticles.summaryEn: Researchers recently tested two new drugs designed to prevent heart disease. Despite high hopes, both medications failed to reduce the number of heart attacks or strokes in patients. One drug targeted inflammation, while the other focused on a specific protein in the blood. quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary biological mechanism by which baxdrostat addresses high blood pressure in patients with primary aldosteronism?

options.A: It surgically removes non-cancerous growths from the adrenal glands.
options.B: It inhibits the production of the hormone that causes the kidneys to retain salt.
options.C: It directly destroys the adrenal glands to stop hormone secretion.
options.D: It replaces existing lifelong daily medications with a temporary treatment.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，baxdrostat 是一種醛固酮合成酶抑制劑 (ASI)，其作用機制是阻斷身體產生導致血壓升高的荷爾蒙（醛固酮），從而防止腎臟過度保留鹽分。選項 A 錯誤，因為手術切除腺體是傳統療法，而非藥物作用；選項 C 錯誤，藥物是抑制荷爾蒙合成，而非直接破壞腺體；選項 D 錯誤，藥物設計初衷是針對難治型高血壓，而非單純為了取代藥物。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might the use of baxdrostat change the way doctors diagnose primary aldosteronism?

options.A: Because the drug is so effective that it eliminates the need for any further medical testing.
options.B: Because the drug can identify the specific gene responsible for the condition.
options.C: Because the drug could serve as a non-invasive alternative to surgery and diagnostic procedures.
options.D: Because the drug is only effective if the patient has already undergone surgery.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段，專家指出如果研究結果獲得證實，醫生未來可能不需要依賴侵入性的診斷程序和手術，而是直接使用 baxdrostat 來觀察病患的反應。這暗示了藥物本身可以作為一種診斷工具。選項 A 太過誇大，藥物無法取代所有醫療測試；選項 B 文章未提及藥物具備識別基因的功能；選項 D 與文章內容矛盾，藥物是為了避免手術，而非手術後的配套措施。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, the phrase 'the medical community remains cautiously optimistic' suggests that experts are:

options.A: Hopeful about the drug's potential but aware that more evidence is needed.
options.B: Certain that the drug will revolutionize medicine despite early failures.
options.C: Worried that the drug will cause more harm than the current treatments.
options.D: Indifferent because they have seen many similar drugs fail in the past.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。Cautiously optimistic（審慎樂觀）意指對某事抱持正面期待，但同時保持警惕，不輕易下定論。文章結尾提到雖然藥物潛力巨大，但仍建議患者在大型研究提供明確證據前，繼續目前的治療。選項 B 錯誤，因為專家並未達到「確信」的程度；選項 C 錯誤，專家並未表示擔憂；選項 D 錯誤，專家雖然提到過去有失敗案例，但對此藥仍抱有期待，而非冷漠。

quiz.question: What is the central message of this article regarding baxdrostat?

options.A: Baxdrostat is the only effective medication currently available for heart disease.
options.B: Surgery remains the most reliable method to cure high blood pressure permanently.
options.C: Baxdrostat shows promise as a potentially curative treatment for a specific type of high blood pressure.
options.D: The medical community has officially declared baxdrostat a total cure for all hypertension.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文旨在介紹 baxdrostat 這款新藥，強調其不僅能管理症狀，還可能透過抑制荷爾蒙甚至消除過度活躍細胞來「治癒」特定類型的原發性醛固酮增多症，這也是文章的核心主題。選項 A 錯誤，文章僅提到該藥針對特定病因；選項 B 錯誤，文章正是強調該藥可能取代手術；選項 D 錯誤，文中專家明確表示現在宣布「完全治癒」還言之過早，且該藥僅針對特定病因，非所有高血壓。
